feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is claimed. Evidence: iterations 0 to 3 show the oval stuck at progress 0.115 and max_error 0.061 m whatever sensing, inertia or track width was tried, so it is probably a fixed feature of that track, not something geometry alone fixes. Iteration 3 (y=0.07 m) gave the best score (51.31) through s-bend progress 0.155, but steering_oscillation rose to 0.127 and 0.138 and line_loss_events returned to 1 on s-bend and slalom, with slalom max_error 0.065 m. I keep the controller at iteration 3 settings, so any change in the next race is attributable to the sensor row. If the next race shows steering_oscillation at or below 0.10 with line_loss_events at 0 and s-bend progress near 0.15 or better, keep y=0.06 m and tune the lead between 0.06 and 0.07 m. If oscillation is still above 0.10 at y=0.06 m, return the row to y=0.05 m. If the s-bend progress falls back to the 0.04 level (iteration 0 to 2 values), the lead is not helping, so keep the lead but change nothing else. Per track, check max_error on the oval, because it has not moved in four iterations.
requested_changes: If steering_oscillation is still above 0.10 at sensor y=0.06 m (iteration 3 gave 0.127 on s-bend and 0.138 on slalom), return sensor_positions y to 0.05 m and keep wheel_track 0.09 m, to test whether the lead is too aggressive.

If line_loss_events is 0 but s-bend progress stays below 0.2 and max_error is at or above 0.06 m (iterations 0 to 3 all show this), change wheel_radius to 0.04 m to raise ground speed. Turn authority changes (iteration 2, wheel_track 0.12 to 0.10 m) did not move max_error, so speed is the next untested lever.

If slalom max_error stays above 0.06 m at y=0.06 m (iteration 3 gave 0.065 m), widen the sensor x spread to +/-0.065 m with sensor_size 0.016, since the 0.05 m spread may let the line leave view on the slalom bends.
